resource.name: Chain Drain: Built Environment White Paper and Research Database
resource.description: Bryan Boyer and Greg Lindsay's University of Michigan white paper and accompanying company database examine losses of information and value between architecture, engineering, construction and operations. Combines practitioner interviews, four futures scenarios and source-linked company dossiers comparing digital automation with changes to the division of work. A reference for institutional learning, built-environment strategy and exploratory sector mapping. Company promises and AI-assisted classifications are not independently verified performance outcomes.
resource.resource_type: Research Report; Research & Reference; Index & Directory
resource.industries: Architecture & Built Environment; Futures & Foresight; Design Management & Business; Academic Research; Research, History & Education
resource.keywords: Chain Drain; Bryan Boyer; Greg Lindsay; University of Michigan; Taubman College; AECO; architecture; construction; operations; institutional learning; knowledge transfer; supply chain; scenarios; strategic design; organizational research; AI-assisted research; company database
resource.audit_note: Author project and current database, selected PDF text, indexed Michigan repository record and Taubman College research coverage reviewed November 11, 2026. Database reports 501 companies/products and a November 8 update; older indexed pages contain smaller samples, so figures must be tied to a version. No independent full-database recount or performance evaluation. The report's main context is the US built environment; scenarios are analytical alternatives, not forecasts. DOI deposit identifies a white paper, not proof of peer review. Dossiers disclose AI drafting and human editing; the sampled Structured AI record identifies sources, access dates and human-edit date. Experimental cluster analysis explicitly relies on model interpretation. No blanket reuse license established. Public reading is not permission to reproduce the database, figures or third-party source material. PDF screenshots and direct downloads failed; figures and layout were not visually verified. The PDF contents heading says version 1.1 while its suggested citation says v1.11; version reconciliation remains unresolved. Some links from the parsed research index resolve with a duplicated research path; a directly addressed sample dossier was readable. No bulk import of company records, source text or graphics.

event.name: Not Here, Not Now: Rethinking Speculative Design
event.description: University-hosted international symposium at Musashino Art University's Ichigaya campus, 7F Co-Creation Space Ma. Features Anthony Dunne and Fiona Raby, followed by a panel on speculative design with participating researcher Paul Gong. The participant announcement gives 18:00-20:45 JST, English without Japanese interpretation, and a public capacity of 40. University calendar corroborates the date and campus. Reservation required; ticket price, remaining places, livestream and recording availability were not verified.
event.source: Official Musashino Art University Ichigaya event-calendar search-index text confirms December 3, 2026, title and 7F venue: https://ichigaya.musabi.ac.jp/event/ . Paul Gong's first-person announcement, indexed within LinkedIn activity at https://uk.linkedin.com/in/gem-barton-45600122 , supplies program, time, language and capacity. The post is by Gong, not by the profile owner. Direct Peatix retrieval failed. Direct university index returned an older subset than its search-index text. Reviewed November 11, 2026; no registration submitted, no cancellation or actual occurrence inferred, and no reuse rights assumed.

research_benchmark: For future institutional case studies, examine what information, responsibility and evidence survives each transfer between funders, commissioners, researchers, delivery teams and evaluators. This is a proposed application to cultural work, not a finding that the built-environment model is already validated for cultural sectors.
verification_limits: Selected PDF text, not a complete independent review of every claim or bibliography item. PDF screenshot rendering and file download failed, so no chart or layout verification claimed.
